solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Artist or doctor at excavation returning a single nail

parts.note: MO is a Medical Officer, a common crossword doctor
to dig is to excavate, and a dig is an archaeological excavation

indicators.note: returning signals that the following words are written back to front

parts.note: a single is one, the Roman numeral I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzling choice between an artist and a doctor at a dig who is going back for one nail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns I + NAIL into LIANI. 'or' is only a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Amedeo Modigliani was an Italian painter and sculptor famous for elongated portraits.

parts.note: the Norse deity's name splits as O (nothing, zero) and DIN (noise), so it looks like 'no noise': not noisy at all

explanation.surface: A short remark that some deity is loud, promptly contradicted.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the name as O + DIN: zero noise, so the god is apparently not noisy.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief god of Norse mythology, father of Thor, is the deity the clue points to.

clue.text: Ask to popular fast in Dijon

parts.note: something popular is said to be in
Dijon is in France, and the French word for fast or quickly is vite

explanation.surface: Someone asks to eat at a trendy fast-food place in Dijon.
explanation.definitionFit: To invite someone is to ask them to come along, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Novel announcing praise for sports hall

indicators.note: announcing means the words are spoken aloud, so we want something that sounds like them

parts.note: to praise is to laud, and a sports hall is a gym; said together they give the sound wanted

explanation.surface: Someone announcing their praise for a new sports hall.
explanation.walkthrough: LAUD + GYM spoken aloud sound like the title; 'for' is part of the run read aloud, not a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Jim is Joseph Conrad's 1900 novel about a disgraced young seaman.

indicators.note: fresh suggests the letters of air are made new, put into another order
a word's opening is its first letter, here taken from doors

explanation.surface: Fresh but dry air coming in as the doors are opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges AIR into ARI; 'opening' takes the D of doors.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid land is parched and dry, lacking moisture: a straight synonym.

clue.text: Furniture store holding bar on flower arranging

indicators.note: holding means one piece contains the other inside it

parts.note: Ikea is the Swedish furniture retailer
to bar something is to ban it

explanation.surface: A furniture shop imposing a ban on flower arranging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' reads as a noun on the surface but works as a verb meaning prohibit; 'on' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikebana is the Japanese art of arranging flowers, the clue's closing phrase.

clue.text: Distributed pay receipt for entertaining turn

indicators.note: distributed means the letters are scattered and laid out again in a new order

explanation.surface: Pay slips handed out to staff before a performer's act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distributed' rearranges the ten letters of PAY RECEIPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A party piece is a set routine someone performs to amuse guests, a turn in the music-hall sense.

clue.text: Wagner's work in talk at assemblies

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another, here within the word for talk

parts.note: gas is idle talk or chatter
The Ring is Wagner's operatic cycle Der Ring des Nibelungen

explanation.surface: Wagner's opera discussed during talks at meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal: the opera cycle sits inside the word for idle chatter. 'at' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Meetings of people, or assemblies, are crowds brought together: a plain synonym.

indicators.note: presented by puts the article after the paper, as if offered by it

parts.note: a rag is a low-grade newspaper
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper presents a feature about music.
explanation.definitionFit: A raga is a melodic framework in Indian classical music, so a kind of music.

parts.note: Long John Silver is the pirate in Treasure Island
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A pirate crew showing off its catch of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: Silverside is a cut of beef from the outer thigh, often salted; 'some' marks it as one example.

clue.text: Discoloration left in badly finished work

indicators.note: in places the letter for left inside the bungled job

parts.note: a botch is a bungled, clumsily finished piece of work

explanation.surface: A stain left on a shoddily finished piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: A blotch is an irregular patch of colour or a stain on a surface, a mark of discoloration.

indicators.note: attacking suggests the letters of maestri are set upon and knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A villainous bird attacking conductors, read as a comic news item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fowl' looks like a bird, but it is the surname of Eoin Colfer's boy master criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemis Fowl is the teenage criminal mastermind who is title character of Eoin Colfer's children's novels.

indicators.note: semi means half, so only the first half of the word for US is kept

parts.note: US stands for American
cement binds bricks or stones together

explanation.surface: A half-American adhesive, read as a product description.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semi' keeps the first four of AMERICAN's eight letters, AMER.
explanation.definitionFit: An amercement is a penalty or monetary fine, an old legal term for a fine imposed at a court's discretion.

definitions.meaning: a playful cricket reading: a duck is a score of nothing, so the phrase hints at scores as a run of zeros on a scoreboard

explanation.surface: An odd cricket statistic: sixty, apparently made of eight ducks.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, so three of them make sixty, the biblical span of years.

indicators.note: of here means taken out of the words that follow, the letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Praise for a celebrated band or orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across famouS ENSEmble.
explanation.definitionFit: A sense of something, such as of humour, is an awareness or appreciation of it.

parts.note: to snap is to break suddenly
per means through or by means of, as in per post

explanation.surface: A turtle making a breakthrough, perhaps escaping its pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is a link, standing for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapping turtle of North America is commonly called a snapper.

clue.text: Discarded items sculpted by artist and priest

parts.note: sc. abbreviates sculpsit, Latin for 'sculpted', seen on statues
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Junk turned into sculpture by an artist and a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap is waste material, items thrown out as no longer useful.

clue.text: Leading Muslims enter city championing Allah

definitions.text: Leading Muslims enter city championing Allah

indicators.note: leading picks the front letter of each word in the clue

explanation.surface: Muslims leading the faithful into a holy city where Allah is upheld.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of the five words spell the answer, and the whole clue describes it too.
explanation.definitionFit: Mecca is the holiest city in Islam, which Muslims enter on pilgrimage to honour God.

indicators.note: mid takes the central letter of the month named

parts.note: cru is a French wine term for a vineyard's growth or vintage

explanation.surface: The colour of a wine harvested in mid-September.
explanation.walkthrough: September has nine letters; its central one is E.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is a pale greyish-yellow, the shade of unbleached linen.

indicators.note: heartless removes the central letter of the girl's name

parts.note: Megan is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A cruel girl who is merely that way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' looks like a description of a cold girl but drops the middle letter G of MEGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden mean is the exact right balance, neither too much nor too little: just so.

clue.text: Newton with one key in pocket

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: in places the musical key inside the word for pocket

parts.note: a sac is a pouch or pocket in an animal or plant
A is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone named Newton carrying a single key in their pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Isaac Newton is the physicist; his first name stands for the surname here.

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
a pack is a group of hunting hounds

explanation.surface: Stolen diamonds sniffed out by dogs inside a coolbox.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is a link: the answer is the thing found in a coolbox.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen gel bag is what keeps the contents of a portable cooler chilled.

clue.text: Whence water in France once spilt round diary

indicators.note: round means the scrambled letters go around the record book
spilt suggests the letters of once are spilled out and rearranged

parts.note: a log is a diary or daily record

explanation.surface: French water spilt over somebody's diary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilt' rearranges the word once, and 'round' wraps that around the diary word. The definition asks where eau came from: the German city.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de Cologne literally means water from Cologne, the German city where the scent was first made.

clue.text: Crack cocaine, note, a bad habit

parts.note: C is slang for cocaine
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a vice is a bad habit

explanation.surface: Crack cocaine described as a vicious habit in a cautionary note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' sits next to cocaine as the drug, but it is the definition: a narrow opening.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevice is a narrow crack or fissure in rock or a wall.

parts.note: a posse is a body of law officers summoned by a sheriff
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A statement that there are officers aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to own or hold it, a straight synonym.

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of dunes are put out of order

explanation.surface: A marsh plant found among sand hills in the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DUNES into SUNDE; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The sundew is a small carnivorous plant of boggy ground that traps insects on sticky hairs.

clue.text: Some help UK company backing rough layout

indicators.note: backing means the selected letters are read from right to left
some means only part of the following words is used

explanation.surface: A British firm supporting another with a rough draft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes PUKCOM from helP UK COMpany; 'backing' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mock-up is a rough model or preliminary layout of a design.

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A token of affection from the men.
explanation.definitionFit: A portent is a sign of what is to come.

indicators.note: suggests here means the remaining letters, said aloud, bring the answer to mind
not half means half of the name is dropped

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of US President Dwight D. Eisenhower

explanation.surface: What time is it, according to Ike? An exclamation, 'Not half!'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' drops EISEN, half of EISENHOWER, leaving HOWER, which said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sixty minutes is a unit of time.

clue.text: Equip hoary tutor with weapons for final battle

parts.note: to arm is to equip with weapons
hoary means old, grey with age
a don is a university tutor

explanation.surface: Instruction to arm an old teacher for a last stand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with weapons' completes the sense of 'Equip' for the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Armageddon is the biblical last conflict between good and evil at the end of the world.

definitions.meaning: ..., the Prayer Book catechism's placeholder letters for a name, offers a choice of two letters
a standard is the usual level or rule

explanation.surface: Picking letters according to a set standard.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as N OR M, the first reading is a choice between two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is the usual or expected level, a standard.

parts.note: murphy is slang for a potato, so a crowned potato suggests a monarch who is also a potato variety

explanation.surface: A man called Murphy being crowned.
explanation.walkthrough: Murphy is informal for a potato, from the Irish surname.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a classic British potato variety named after a king, so a potato on the throne.
